subject: Instrumentation Ownership Workshop — dashboards, trace hooks & alert routing
messages:
From: Jordan Miller <jmiller@acme.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme.acmecorp.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Observability kickoff + goals for instrumentation ownership

Sean / Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move from pilot to production in Q1 and would like to lock down who owns what for dashboards, tracing hooks, and alert routing so our SREs can take on day-to-day ops. High level asks from our side: 

- A mapping of dashboards -> owner (Redwood vs Acme)
- Trace hook patterns we should standardize in our services (examples + minimal schema)
- Alert routing matrix (alerts -> escalation path)

Can we run a 60–90 minute workshop next week to walk the teams through the proposed mappings and produce an action tracker? I'm attaching our current dashboard inventory to give context.

Attachments: acme_dashboard_inventory.xlsx (spreadsheet listing ~24 dashboards)

Thanks,
Jordan Miller
Director, Platform Reliability
Acme Robotics

From: sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miller <jmiller@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability kickoff + goals for instrumentation ownership

Jordan —

Appreciate the inventory — that's perfect context. We can run a focused workshop. Proposed agenda (60–75 minutes):

1) Quick alignment (10m): scope / success criteria for production handoff
2) Dashboard inventory review (15m): identify duplicates, ownership candidates
3) Trace hook patterns (15m): examine 2 service examples + propose schema
4) Alert routing matrix (15m): map alerts to oncall / CS / SE / Redwood support
5) Action tracker and owners (10m)

Prep we'll bring: a trace-hook-template.md with recommended headers/payload, and a starter alert-routing spreadsheet. Can you confirm internal SREs who should attend? If the 60–75m window is tight, we can follow up with a 30m deep-dive on tracing after the main session.

I can run the session Thursday 12/10 10:00–11:15 PT or Friday 12/11 09:00–10:15 PT. Which works?

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Sean — Thursday 12/10 10:00–11:15 PT works for us. I'll include two folks from our SRE team: Maya Patel (m.patel@acme.com) and Rafael Mendes (r.mendes@acme.com). Ops team will be on standby.

One request from my lead: can we try to produce a single "ownership matrix" during the session that lists: dashboard, owner, Redwood playbook link (if Redwood-owned), and handoff acceptance criteria? That will speed our go/no-go conversations.

I'll drop a calendar invite and attach the dashboard inventory you referenced.

From: sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Prep for Acme instrumentation ownership workshop (12/10)

Team —

Quick internal plan so we roll into the session with clear deliverables. Jordan confirmed 12/10 10:00–11:15 PT and will include two SREs. Goals: produce an ownership matrix for dashboards, agree on trace-hook minimal schema, and draft an alert-routing matrix with at least primary + fallback contacts.

Action items (assignments below):
- Marissa: bring the trace-hook-template.md and two example service traces we can walk through (prefer one sync-service and one async-worker). Preload examples to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmeOnboarding
- Ben: prepare starter alert-routing spreadsheet (map 12 high-priority alerts -> default owner, escalation step, Redwood contact). Put a column for SLA target and handoff acceptance test.
- Laura: create ownership-matrix template (columns: dashboard, suggested owner, playbook link, acceptance criteria). We'll use this live in the session and capture committed owners.
- Me: facilitate, run agenda, and capture the ops-action-tracker.csv (I will maintain it during the session).

Attachments I'll upload now: trace-hook-template.md, ops-action-tracker.csv (empty tracker). Jordan attached the dashboard inventory which I've copied into the folder.

Timing note: if we don't finish trace schema discussion on the 10th we'll schedule a follow-up 30m tracing deep-dive the week after (preferably Mon 12/13).

Thanks — I'll share the calendar link and a short pre-read tomorrow.

—Sean

From: Jordan Miller <jmiller@acme.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme.acmecorp.com
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability kickoff + goals for instrumentation ownership

Thanks — confirmed on our side. Quick logistical notes for the session:

- I'll share screen for the dashboard inventory and we can edit Laura's template live.
- Our SREs will expect the trace-hook-template.md (please link the file in the invite).
- For alert routing, start with the 12-high-priority list (included in the inventory under tab "critical_alerts").

If you can add a short list of acceptance criteria examples to Laura's template before the workshop (e.g., alert noise < 5% false positives in 7 days; dashboard coverage for each customer-facing flow >= 90%), that will help us make decisions quickly.

See you Thursday 12/10.

Jordan
Director, Platform Reliability
Acme Robotics
